educationalGoal: Psychological information processing is grounded in the brain’s electrical activity. This course introduces EEG- and MEG-based brain-informatics approaches to examine the temporal dynamics of psychological processes, focusing on what these methods can and cannot measure. advice:
This course introduces the basics of brain information science using EEG and MEG to study fundamental psychological processes such as perception, attention, and cognition. Students learn what EEG/MEG can measure and their limitations, the principles of signal generation and data acquisition, and gain perspectives for understanding research on neural rhythms, event-related potentials, and higher-order brain functions.

This course is subject to the course credit system.
requiredKnowledge: Students should have a review of Perceptual and Cognitive Psychology and Introduction to Psychology. It is desirable that students have taken Neuro-Physiological Psychology.

achievementLevels.ideal: Students acquire a thorough understanding of psychological information-processing processes such as attention, memory, emotion, and cognitive control, based on brain-informatics approaches centered on electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG), including how these processes are generated and change over time. In addition, they can explain and critically evaluate the potential applications of these approaches to information and interface design that are adapted to human psychological information-processing characteristics, while taking into account the meanings and limitations of indices such as event-related potentials and neural oscillations.
achievementLevels.standard: Students understand the fundamental principles of measurement and analysis using electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG) in relation to psychological information-processing processes such as attention, memory, emotion, and cognitive control, and can explain how these indices are associated with specific psychological processes. In addition, students can understand the principles of information design that take human psychological information-processing characteristics into account, based on findings from brain informatics.

              Psychological information processing is grounded in the brain’s electrical activity. This course introduces EEG- and MEG-based brain-informatics approaches to examine the temporal dynamics of psychological processes, focusing on what these methods can and cannot measure. Through studies of neural oscillations and event-related potentials, students develop a foundational perspective on brain-informatics–based psychology.

              授業の概要および学習上の助言

              This course introduces the basics of brain information science using EEG and MEG to study fundamental psychological processes such as perception, attention, and cognition. Students learn what EEG/MEG can measure and their limitations, the principles of signal generation and data acquisition, and gain perspectives for understanding research on neural rhythms, event-related potentials, and higher-order brain functions.

This course is subject to the course credit system.
